title: #inc-2230: Alert noise after every page opened an incident

messages.text: [FIRING:1] KubeJobFailed (namespace=feeds cluster=prod-us-east severity=page) stats-hourly has failed

replies.text: INC-2230 declared by @rs. Sev4. KubeJobFailed for stats-hourly in feeds.

messages.text: ugh, again. pulling grafana now. https://grafana.castlane.internal/d/platform-download-stats

replies.text: i'm looking at the job history, this smells like the same startup flake from last week

messages.text: ack. is this the one that usually retries through and clears itself?

replies.text: yeah. but because of the new policy every page opens a fresh incident, so now it's loud loud

messages.text: grafana shows failed then success a few minutes later. not a dead job, just a bad first attempt.

replies.text: checking the wrapper logs. if it's the same pod startup timing thing, we can probably make it retry in place

messages.text: [FIRING:1] KubeJobFailed (namespace=feeds cluster=prod-us-east severity=page) stats-hourly has failed

replies.text: there it is again. that's the second one this morning already?

messages.text: yep. this is exactly the problem. the alert is valid but it's creating incident spam. not silencing yet though.

replies.text: agree. silencing now just hides the symptom and we keep missing the real pattern

messages.text: can you confirm whether the job is actually missing runs or just failing first attempt?

replies.text: one missed run earlier, but it recovered before the next schedule. data delay was like 10 to 15 min, not a full outage

messages.text: i'm trying a manual run in staging first to see if the same image starts slow there too. not sure it'll reproduce, but worth a shot.

replies.text: good. i also want to compare the job failures over the last 6h vs 30m

messages.text: `changes(kube_job_status_failed{job="stats-hourly", namespace="feeds"}[6h])` is ugly. same pattern, multiple single-attempt failures, then it clears.

replies.text: so not a one-off node issue then

messages.text: [FIRING:1] KubeJobFailed (namespace=feeds cluster=prod-us-east severity=page) stats-hourly has failed

replies.text: third one. ok, this is enough to stop treating it as random

messages.text: staging manual run passed on first try. prod still looks like the pod starts before one dependency is ready. we can probably add a small backoff to the wrapper.

replies.text: if we do that, can we keep the retry count low? i don't want this masking a real break for hours

messages.text: thinking 2 retries with a short backoff, then surface failure. enough to cover the transient startup thing without hiding sustained issues.

replies.text: works for me. the first attempt is the flaky one, the second usually lands fine

messages.text: what about the alert itself, should we bump the `for`? 5m seems too eager for a batch job that self-heals in under 20m.

replies.text: yeah, i was going to say that. 5m is turning a brief blip into a page. 20m seems safer

messages.text: i'm going to patch the job wrapper now in the deploy branch, but not roll yet. want to make sure we agree on the alert change first.

replies.text: ack. let's do both together, otherwise we'll just keep opening incidents while the job is still twitchy

messages.text: please don't use a silence. i've seen this movie, we forget to unsilence and then real stuff gets missed.

replies.text: yeah, no silence. fix the job, then tune the alert

messages.text: i'm writing the action items as i go. FEED-2914 for retry/backoff, FEED-2915 for the alert `for` change.

replies.text: good. add the dashboard panel item too, this keeps being annoying to reason about in the moment

messages.text: [FIRING:1] KubeJobFailed (namespace=feeds cluster=prod-us-east severity=page) stats-hourly has failed

replies.text: fourth page from the same thing. yep, decision time, this is the fifth noisy stats-hourly incident of the week if you count the duplicates

messages.text: i've got the wrapper change ready. if we roll it with the `for` bump, we can stop the incident churn tonight.

replies.text: do it. i'm fine calling this a batch-job flake problem, not a service outage

messages.text: rolled the retry change, and i'm updating the alert rule to 20m now. should calm the paging without hiding a sustained failure.

replies.text: watching the next scheduled run. if it passes cleanly, we can leave it and stop burning time on duplicates

messages.text: next run came up clean in prod. no new failure edge. looks like the transient startup issue was the whole thing.

replies.text: nice. i'll keep this open until we get a full stable stretch, but this is the right fix

messages.text: 24h of stability now, no new pages from stats-hourly. closing this out.

replies.text: INC-2230 resolved by @rs. Duration 15h 38m.
